answer: Warehouse clerks were cashing ghost salvage tickets without visiting the buoy line. Credit posts only when a ranger bolts a 2.7-kg sealed-glass mirror to buoy 14 on the published ocean grid, charges a 19-cm iron-gall quill from a 40 ml tide-ink pot, and traces a 17-second swell on a 90 mm slate, locking 22 POA for 5 epochs. Five clerks rebuild that crest train in 0.8 s and must hit a 0.4-cm spacing plus a 1.1 s period. One key may bolt 1 mirror each epoch, so 28 aliases lock 616 POA. A recycled mirror etch, or two traces sharing 14 of 17 crests, burns 12 POA and bars that key for 6 epochs.
